    ## 2. Architecture and state
    
    Use Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and `lucide-react`, with static deployment on Vercel.
    
    ### Application structure
    
    - **Routes (`src/app`):** `/` for Dashboard, plus `/welcome`, `/chores`, `/expenses`, `/agreements` and `/settings`. A client initialization gate shows loading until storage is read, then presents setup, recovery or the requested screen.
    - **Shared UI (`src/components`, `src/styles`):** App shell, page header, avatar/picker, fields, status pills, accessible dialogs, confirmations, notices and empty states. Desktop sidebar; mobile navigation drawer. Tables become cards on phones; Kanban scrolls within its own region.
    - **Feature modules (`src/features`):** Setup, household, chores, expenses, agreements and dashboard. Keep form drafts local to their feature.
    - **Domain utilities (`src/domain`):** Types, runtime validation, money parsing/allocation, balances, rotation, date helpers and sample generation. These functions must not depend on React or browser storage.
    - **State layer (`src/state`):** One client provider with typed domain actions and shared selectors. Route changes must preserve the provider. Keep browser storage access behind a small adapter.
    
    Follow the PRD's `AppState` model with `schemaVersion: 1`. Use stable IDs and member ordering; retain archived members. Persist facts, selected profile and settings. Calculate balances, transfer suggestions, overdue indicators and dashboard counts from those facts.
    
    ### Important interfaces
    
    - Domain actions cover CRUD, status changes, rotation, archive/restore, profile selection and resets.
    - Commands return success or actionable validation/storage errors.
    - Storage exposes load, save and clear operations with explicit failure results.
    - Inject time and ID generation into domain operations where needed for deterministic tests.
    
    ### Financial rules
    
    - Parse currency input as decimal strings into integer cents; percentages into integer basis points.
    - Require safe integer amounts and reject inputs whose calculations exceed supported integer bounds.
    - Allocate equal-split remainder cents by stable roster order. Use largest remainder for percentages, with the same stable tie-breaker.
    - Validate payer and participant totals independently. Reject duplicate entries for the same member within each role.
    - Generate advisory transfers from open-expense nets, matching largest balances first with stable member-ID ties.
    - Settlement is a confirmed whole-expense marker for resolution outside the app, never an integrated payment action.
    
    ## 3. Persistence and recovery
    
    Use only `localStorage["roomieos:v1"]`.
    
    - Read storage once after client mount. Do not render household-dependent content or save defaults before initialization completes.
    - Distinguish absent data, valid data, malformed/unsupported data and unavailable storage.
    - Validate structure, references, roster constraints, dates and financial invariants on load and before persistence.
    - Generate sample data only after explicit selection or confirmed reset. Base dates on the local date at that moment.
    - For each change, calculate and validate the next state, persist it, then publish it to React. Show success only after saving succeeds.
    - If saving fails, preserve the prior household and the user's form input. Show a useful error and allow retry.
    - Invalid data remains untouched until the user confirms reset. Unsupported versions must not silently become sample data.
    - Reset demo replaces saved state only after confirmation. Start over clears it only after confirmation and successful storage removal.
    - On another tab's storage change, stop stale writes and offer reload before further editing.
    - Store calendar dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`; use timestamps for completion events. Recompute date-sensitive displays on focus and relevant interactions.

    ## 5. Dependencies, tests and risks
    
    ### Dependencies
    
    Next.js, React, React DOM, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Lucide. Add Zod for runtime validation and Vitest for domain/storage tests. Use native forms and native dialogs with tested focus handling. Avoid state libraries, chart packages, remote fonts and UI frameworks. Select compatible stable package versions during scaffolding and commit the lockfile.
    
    Foundation tooling also includes Playwright for real-browser layout/navigation/dialog checks and Prettier for source formatting. Milestone 2 adds Zod 4.6.7 as a direct runtime dependency. TypeScript is pinned to 6.0.3 because the installed Next.js lint tooling rejects TypeScript 7; ESLint 9 matches the upstream React plugin's supported peer range. Exact dependency versions are recorded in `package-lock.json`.
    
    ### Required verification
    
    - **Money:** 100 cents across three participants yields 34/33/33; multiple payers; percentage rounding/ties; fixed totals; invalid inputs; zero-sum nets; deterministic transfers; settlement/reopening.
    - **Chores:** Completion identity/time; repeated completion without duplicate events for unchanged status; preserved history; rotation wraparound and archived members; yesterday/today comparisons.
    - **State/storage:** Sample and empty initialization; malformed/unsupported payloads; failed reads/writes/clears; roster limits; archive guards; currency blocked by any expenses.
    - **Browser:** Refresh every major flow, switch perspective, cancel dialogs, keyboard navigation/focus restoration, error feedback and every visible action.
    - **Layout:** 375, 768 and 1280 px; contained board scrolling; usable expense forms and dialogs.
    - **Release:** Lint, typecheck, tests and production build; deployed deep links and private-window first-run behavior.
    
    ### Main risks and mitigations
    
    | Risk | Mitigation |
    |---|---|
    | Expense-form complexity and rounding | Implement pure tested arithmetic first; preview exact contributions/shares before save |
    | Storage hydration and data loss | Client initialization gate, runtime validation, explicit recovery and save-before-publish |
    | Archived historical references | Retain member records and stable order; guard reopening and new assignments |
    | Dialog accessibility and mobile density | Reuse shared primitives; check keyboard, focus and small viewports early |
    | Short deadline | Small milestones; prioritize correct required behavior; defer optional visuals/uploads |

    ## 1. Design intent
    
    **One sentence:** RoomieOS should feel like a thoughtfully designed shared notebook that happens to calculate expenses and manage chores.
    
    Take inspiration from Notion's clarity: a paper-like work surface, restrained typography, predictable navigation, compact metadata and generous content spacing. Do **not** imitate Notion's logos, brand assets, exact layouts or microcopy. RoomieOS has its own identity, tailored around household coordination.
    
    **Use visual restraint.** The content is the product; UI decoration should never compete with it. No glossy gradient dashboards, giant illustrations, game UI, neon badges, or unnecessary animations.
    
    ### Principles
    1. **Readability before flair:** Clear text hierarchy; prominent page title; one primary action per screen.
    2. **Friendly but useful:** Natural language and small moments of warmth; no forced jokes.
    3. **Low cognitive load:** Strong defaults, few mandatory fields, visible next steps.
    4. **Consistent views:** A chore looks like the same item in list, Kanban, and dashboard.
    5. **Trustworthy financial UI:** Expose exact splits and payer contributions; never hide math behind a mystery number.
    6. **Accessible by default:** Keyboard support, visible focus, contrast, non-color status labels and mobile tap targets.
    
    ## 2. Visual reference and identity
    
    **Logo/wordmark:** A small rounded square containing a simplified `R` or house outline, followed by **RoomieOS**. Use local SVG/CSS, not a remotely hosted image. Tagline on welcome screen: *Your shared home, organized.*
    
    **Illustration approach:** None required. Use avatars (initials, icon/emoji or uploaded thumbnails), simple Lucide icons and subtle surfaces. A small house glyph next to the household name is enough to communicate context.
    
    **Application voice:** Plain, supportive, concise. Examples:
    - `Good afternoon, Avery` (optional greeting, no hard-coded time assumptions)
    - `Your chores` / `Everyone's expenses` / `House agreements`
    - `No chores assigned to you. You're all caught up.`
    - `This expense is settled. It no longer affects outstanding balances.`
    - `Saved on this browser only` (visible in Settings or first-run helper)
    
    ## 3. Design tokens
    
    Use these as CSS custom properties in `src/styles/tokens.css` (or equivalent Tailwind theme mapping). Preserve relative hierarchy if token syntax differs.
    
    ### Colors — light theme
    
    | Token | Hex | Purpose |
    |---|---|---|
    | `--bg-page` | `#FFFFFF` | Main canvas |
    | `--bg-sidebar` | `#F7F7F5` | Navigation rail |
    | `--bg-subtle` | `#F9F9F8` | Gentle panels / hover base |
    | `--bg-hover` | `#EFEFED` | Interactive hover |
    | `--bg-selected` | `#E9EFFC` | Selected navigation / selected control |
    | `--text-primary` | `#37352F` | Main text |
    | `--text-secondary` | `#787774` | Secondary text / supporting labels |
    | `--text-tertiary` | `#9B9A97` | Placeholders / metadata |
    | `--border` | `#E9E9E7` | Fine dividers, controls |
    | `--border-strong` | `#D9D9D6` | Active field outlines |
    | `--accent` | `#315D9D` | Primary action / active navigation / links |
    | `--accent-hover` | `#264A7D` | Primary action hover |
    | `--focus` | `#315D9D` | Keyboard focus ring |
    | `--success` | `#24735B` | Completed / settled |
    | `--success-bg` | `#EAF5F0` | Completed badges |
    | `--warning` | `#9A6017` | Due soon / skipped |
    | `--warning-bg` | `#FFF3E4` | Warning badges |
    | `--danger` | `#B64747` | Overdue / destructive |
    | `--danger-bg` | `#FBEAEA` | Overdue backgrounds |
    
    **Color behavior:** Default body text is charcoal, not pure black. Use blue sparingly for important interactive elements. Prefer neutral borders over excessive shadows. Never rely on red/green alone: always show a readable status label.
    
    ### Typography
    
    - **Font:** `Inter`, if available locally/system-installed; otherwise `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. Avoid making the app dependent on a remote font.
    - **Body:** 14 px / 1.55; main content can use 15–16 px when appropriate.
    - **Large page title:** 30 px / 1.2 / weight 700 (mobile 26 px).
    - **Section title:** 18 px / 1.3 / weight 650.
    - **Card title / emphasis:** 14–15 px / weight 600.
    - **Overline / metadata:** 12 px / weight 500 / muted.
    - **Financial numbers:** 24–28 px / weight 650; tabular numeral feature.
    - **Buttons / nav:** 13–14 px / 500–600.
    - **Never:** all-caps paragraphs or decorative, heavy display fonts.
    
    ### Geometry and spacing
    
    - **Spacing unit:** 4 px. Preferred gaps: 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40 px.
    - **Sidebar:** 248 px wide on desktop; subtle right border.
    - **Top bar:** ~56 px high; breadcrumb/location on left, active roommate switcher on right.
    - **Main max width:** 1120 px with 40 px horizontal interior padding desktop, 20 px tablet, 16 px phone.
    - **Card radius:** 10 px; **controls radius:** 7 px; **modal radius:** 12 px.
    - **Buttons:** min height 36 px desktop; tap targets >=44 px on touch layouts.
    - **Borders:** 1 px subtle divider; low contrast. **Shadows:** almost none (optional small dialog shadow only).

    import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from "react";
    
    type Variant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger";
    export function buttonStyles(
      variant: Variant = "primary",
      className = "",
      size: "default" | "icon" = "default",
    ) {
      const variants: Record<Variant, string> = {
        primary: "border-transparent bg-accent text-white hover:bg-accent-hover",
        secondary: "border-line-strong bg-page text-ink hover:bg-subtle",
        ghost: "border-transparent text-muted hover:bg-hover hover:text-ink",
        danger: "border-transparent bg-danger text-white hover:brightness-90",
      };
      const spacing = size === "icon" ? "size-11 shrink-0 p-0" : "px-4 py-2";
      return `inline-flex min-h-11 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-[7px] border text-sm font-medium transition-colors disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 ${spacing} ${variants[variant]} ${className}`;
    }
    
    export function Button({
      variant = "primary",
      className,
      type = "button",
      size = "default",
      ...props
    }: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & {
      variant?: Variant;
      size?: "default" | "icon";
    }) {
      return (
        <button
          type={type}
          className={buttonStyles(variant, className, size)}
          {...props}
        />
      );
    }

      ...props
    }: SelectHTMLAttributes<HTMLSelectElement> & {
      id: string;
      label: string;
      help?: string;
      error?: string;
      children: ReactNode;
    }) {
      return (
        <div className="space-y-2">
          <label htmlFor={id} className="block text-sm font-medium">
            {label}
          </label>
          <div className="relative">
            <select
              {...props}
              id={id}
              className={`${controlStyles} appearance-none pr-10`}
              aria-invalid={error ? true : props["aria-invalid"]}
              aria-describedby={
                [
                  help && `${id}-help`,
                  error && `${id}-error`,
                  props["aria-describedby"],
                ]
                  .filter(Boolean)
                  .join(" ") || undefined
              }
            >
              {children}
            </select>
            <ChevronDown
              aria-hidden="true"
              className="pointer-events-none absolute top-1/2 right-3 size-4 -translate-y-1/2 text-muted"
            />
          </div>
          {help && (
            <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted">
              {help}
            </p>
          )}
          {error && (
            <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-danger">
              {error}
            </p>
          )}
        </div>
      );
    }
    "use client";
    
    import { useEffect, useId, useRef, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import { X } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./button";
    import { InlineNotice } from "./inline-notice";
    
    type DialogProps = {
      open: boolean;
      onClose: () => void;
      title: string;
      description?: string;
      children: ReactNode;
      variant?: "modal" | "drawer";
      id?: string;
      size?: "default" | "wide";
    };
    
    export function Dialog({
      open,
      onClose,
      title,
      description,
      children,
      variant = "modal",
      id,
      size = "default",
    }: DialogProps) {
      const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);
      const titleId = useId();
      const descriptionId = useId();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const dialog = dialogRef.current;
        if (!dialog || !open) return;
        const trigger =
          document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement
            ? document.activeElement
            : null;
        dialog.showModal();
        return () => {
          dialog.close();
          if (trigger?.isConnected) trigger.focus();
        };
      }, [open]);
    
      return (
        <dialog
          ref={dialogRef}
          id={id}
          aria-labelledby={titleId}
          aria-describedby={description ? descriptionId : undefined}
          onCancel={(event) => {
            event.preventDefault();
            onClose();
          }}
          className={`fixed flex-col overflow-hidden border border-line bg-page p-0 text-ink shadow-xl ${variant === "drawer" ? "inset-y-0 left-0 m-0 h-dvh max-h-dvh w-80 max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] rounded-r-xl" : `inset-0 m-auto max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] rounded-xl ${size === "wide" ? "max-w-2xl" : "max-w-lg"}`}`}
        >
          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-between gap-4 border-b border-line px-5 py-3">
            <h2 id={titleId} className="min-w-0 break-words text-lg font-semibold">
              {title}
            </h2>
            <Button
              variant="ghost"
              onClick={onClose}
              aria-label={`Close ${title}`}
              title="Close"
              size="icon"
            >
              <X aria-hidden="true" className="size-5" />
            </Button>
          </div>
          <div className="overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-5">
            {description && (
              <p id={descriptionId} className="mb-5 break-words text-sm text-muted">
                {description}
              </p>
            )}
            {children}
          </div>
        </dialog>
      );
    }
    
    export function ConfirmDialog({
      open,
      onClose,
      onConfirm,
      title,
      description,
      confirmLabel,
      destructive = false,
      error,
    }: Omit<DialogProps, "children" | "variant" | "id"> & {
      onConfirm: () => void;
      confirmLabel: string;
      destructive?: boolean;
      error?: string;
    }) {
      return (
        <Dialog
          open={open}
          onClose={onClose}
          title={title}
          description={description}
        >
          {error && (
            <div className="mb-4">
              <InlineNotice tone="error">{error}</InlineNotice>
            </div>
          )}
          <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-end gap-3">
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button
              variant={destructive ? "danger" : "primary"}
              onClick={onConfirm}
            >
              {confirmLabel}
            </Button>
          </div>
        </Dialog>
      );
    }

## Assistant

**I recommend shadcn/ui for RoomieOS, with HeroUI as the strongest alternative.** Both can give us polished controls while fitting the existing React, TypeScript, and Tailwind stack.

I checked the current components too: buttons already have custom styling, while dropdowns use native `<select>` menus and dialogs use native `<dialog>`. The biggest improvement would come from a consistent treatment of dropdowns, date pickers, menus, forms, and dialogs.

These are the options worth exploring. Visual impressions and migration effort are my assessments for this repository.

| Option | Look and strengths | Tradeoff for RoomieOS | Examples to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| **shadcn/ui — best overall fit** | Clean, restrained components. Component source lives in our project, so we can tailor it closely to RoomieOS’s colors, spacing, and typography. | We maintain the copied component code and review upstream changes ourselves. Moderate migration effort. | [Overview](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs), [Select](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/select), [Dialog](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dialog) |
| **HeroUI — best for a more expressive refresh** | Styled components with rounded surfaces, animations, and polished interaction details. Built on Tailwind v4 and React Aria, including keyboard and focus support. | Its visual defaults would need some restraint to match the current notebook-inspired design. Moderate migration effort. | [Overview](https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/getting-started), [Select](https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/select), [Modal](https://heroui.com/en/docs/react/components/modal) |
| **Mantine — best comprehensive toolkit** | Broad selection of ready-made controls, including searchable selects, menus, modals, and drawers. Has an official Next.js integration guide. | Introduces its own theming/styling conventions alongside our Tailwind setup. I expect more integration work than shadcn. | [Components](https://mantine.dev/core/package/), [Select](https://mantine.dev/core/select/), [Modal](https://mantine.dev/core/modal/) |
| **React Aria Components — best for a fully custom design** | Provides accessible interaction behavior and supports Tailwind styling. Strong foundation for custom selectors, calendars, and dialogs. | Ships without default styles, so more visual design work falls to us. Highest styling effort here. | [Interactive examples](https://react-aria.adobe.com/), [Styling approach](https://react-aria.adobe.com/styling) |

Shadcn’s source ownership is documented in its [introduction](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs). Mantine’s separate styling approach is described in its [CSS documentation](https://mantine.dev/styles/css-modules/).

**I would choose shadcn/ui using its Base UI foundation.** Base UI is now its default, with Radix still supported. That gives us a current starting point without needing to introduce multiple component foundations. [Official announcement](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-07-base-ui-default).

For RoomieOS, I would apply it in this order:

1. **Dropdowns and pickers:** roommate/profile, avatar, currency, category, status, and filters.
2. **Dialogs and action menus:** consistent overlays, spacing, confirmation actions, and mobile behavior.
3. **Buttons and form controls:** cohesive sizing, focus, disabled, selected, and error states.
4. **Date pickers and finishing details:** then review typography, density, and spacing across screens.

The existing shared component structure makes an incremental migration practical. We would still need to verify keyboard behavior, nested overlays, mobile layouts, and existing form validation after replacing controls.

I also checked **daisyUI**. It is useful for quick CSS styling, but its standard [Select component](https://daisyui.com/components/select/) still uses native `<select>`, so it addresses less of what you dislike.

**Start by comparing shadcn’s Select/Dialog demos with HeroUI’s Select/Modal demos.** Shadcn is my choice for a refined evolution of RoomieOS; HeroUI is worth choosing if you prefer a softer, more animated visual direction.

                <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="size-[18px] shrink-0" />
                {label}

      );

    export function ProfileSwitcher() {
      const { state, store, conflict } = useReadyHousehold();
      const members = activeMembers(state);
      const selected = members.find(
        (member) => member.id === state.selectedMemberId,
      )!;
      return (
        <div className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2">
          <MemberAvatar
            name={selected.name}
            icon={
              selected.avatar.kind === "icon" ? selected.avatar.value : undefined
            }
          />
          <label className="min-w-0">
            <span className="block text-xs text-muted">Demo perspective</span>
            <span className="relative block">
              <select
                aria-label="Switch demo perspective"
                value={selected.id}
                disabled={conflict}
                onChange={(event) =>
                  store.dispatch(
                    { type: "select-member", id: event.target.value },
                    "Demo perspective changed.",
                  )
                }
                className="min-h-11 w-32 max-w-full appearance-none truncate rounded pr-6 text-sm font-medium sm:w-40"
              >
                {members.map((member) => (
                  <option key={member.id} value={member.id}>
                    {member.name}
                  </option>
                ))}
              </select>
              <ChevronDown
                aria-hidden="true"
                className="pointer-events-none absolute top-1/2 right-1 size-4 -translate-y-1/2 text-muted"
              />
            </span>
          </label>
        </div>
      );
    }
    import type { InputHTMLAttributes } from "react";
    
    export const controlStyles =
      "w-full min-w-0 rounded-[7px] border border-control bg-page px-3 py-2.5 text-base text-ink aria-invalid:border-danger disabled:bg-subtle";
    
    export function FormField({
      label,
      help,
      error,
      id,
      ...props
    }: InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement> & {
      id: string;
      label: string;
      help?: string;
      error?: string;
    }) {
      const descriptions =
        [help && `${id}-help`, error && `${id}-error`, props["aria-describedby"]]
          .filter(Boolean)
          .join(" ") || undefined;
      return (
        <div className="space-y-2">
          <label htmlFor={id} className="block break-words text-sm font-medium">
            {label}
            {props.required && <span className="text-muted"> (required)</span>}
          </label>
          <input
            {...props}
            id={id}
            className={`${controlStyles} ${props.className ?? ""}`}
            aria-invalid={error ? true : props["aria-invalid"]}
            aria-describedby={descriptions}
          />
          {help && (
            <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted">
              {help}
            </p>
          )}
          {error && (
            <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-danger">
              {error}
            </p>
          )}
        </div>
      );
    }

    function AgreementActions({
      agreement,
      disabled,
      onEdit,
      onDelete,
    }: {
      agreement: Agreement;
      disabled: boolean;
      onEdit: () => void;
      onDelete: () => void;
    }) {
      const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
      const container = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
      const panelId = useId();
      const focusTrigger = () =>
        container.current
          ?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("[data-agreement-trigger]")
          ?.focus();
      useEffect(() => {
        if (!open) return;
        const closeOutside = (event: PointerEvent) => {
          if (
            event.target instanceof Node &&
            !container.current?.contains(event.target)
          )
            setOpen(false);
        };
        document.addEventListener("pointerdown", closeOutside);
        return () => document.removeEventListener("pointerdown", closeOutside);
      }, [open]);
      function choose(callback: () => void) {
        setOpen(false);
        focusTrigger();
        callback();
      }
      return (
        <div
          ref={container}
          className="relative shrink-0"
          onKeyDown={(event) => {
            if (event.key === "Escape" && open) {
              event.preventDefault();
              event.stopPropagation();
              setOpen(false);
              focusTrigger();
            }
          }}
          onBlur={(event) => {
            if (!event.currentTarget.contains(event.relatedTarget)) setOpen(false);

              <Button

    ---
    title: Server and Client Components
    description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.
    related:
      title: Next Steps
      description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.
      links:
        - app/api-reference/directives/use-client
        - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary
    ---
    
    By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.
    
    This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.
    
    > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).
    
    ## When to use Server and Client Components?
    
    The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.
    
    Use **Client Components** when you need:
    
    - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.
    - [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.
    - Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `navigator.geolocation`, etc.
    - [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).
    
    Use **Server Components** when you need:
    
    - Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.
    - Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.
    - Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.
    - Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.
    
    For example, the `<Page>` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `<LikeButton>` which handles client-side interactivity.
    
    ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,17} switcher

    import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
    
    export default async function Page({
      params,
    }: {
      params: Promise<{ id: string }>
    }) {
      const { id } = await params
      const post = await getPost(id)
    
      return (
        <div>
          <main>
            <h1>{post.title}</h1>
            {/* ... */}
            <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
          </main>
        </div>
      )
    }
    ```

## Assistant

The app has a shared UI layer, so most replacements can flow through all screens without changing household logic. I also found separate profile switching, agreement menus, and choice controls that need explicit migration.

The plan will preserve RoomieOS’s palette and layouts, replace shared controls throughout, and defer custom calendars. Two details need care: shadcn’s color-token names overlap ours, and custom selects need new form handlers and browser-test interactions.

## Plan

# RoomieOS: shadcn UI refresh before release

## Summary

Add a focused UI milestone between completed Milestone 5 and release verification. Replace shared navigation and controls throughout the app, producing a consistent first pass for your visual review and later component-specific requests.

Keep RoomieOS’s warm neutral surfaces, blue accent, Lucide icons, typography, and existing page layouts. Use shadcn/ui with Base UI primitives. Desktop navigation starts expanded and can collapse to an icon rail; smaller screens use a slide-over menu.

## Current foundation and replacement map

The app already centralizes buttons, fields, selects, and dialogs. The shell, profile switcher, and agreement menus have separate implementations that also need migration.

| Current implementation | First-pass replacement |
|---|---|
| Custom fixed sidebar and mobile native dialog | Shadcn Sidebar composition with mobile Sheet |
| Shared styled buttons and separate action buttons | Shadcn Button with consistent variants and sizes |
| Native selects, including profile switching | Shadcn Select with grouped options and member avatars where relevant |
| Native dialogs and shared confirmations | Shadcn Dialog and Alert Dialog |
| Custom agreement action disclosure | Shadcn Dropdown Menu |
| Text inputs, textareas, native checkboxes/radios | Shadcn Input, Textarea, Checkbox, Radio Group, and Label |
| Chore view and expense split buttons | Single-selection Toggle Group |
| Native date inputs | Retain date behavior; apply the refreshed input styling |

Cards, tables, badges, avatars, dashboard composition, and Kanban structure retain their current designs. Custom calendars and broader page redesigns belong to subsequent review requests.

## Implementation sequence

### 1. Establish the component foundation

- Configure shadcn for the existing Next.js, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind v4 application. Add only components and dependencies needed by this pass.
- Keep generated component source local and use Base UI consistently for interactive primitives.
- Map shadcn colors to the existing RoomieOS palette. Resolve overlapping names such as `accent`, `sidebar`, and `border` explicitly so existing feature styling retains its meaning.
- Standardize control borders, rounded corners, hover/pressed states, focus rings, disabled states, and validation styling. Maintain 44px touch targets and readable mobile input text.
- Use subtle overlay transitions and honor reduced-motion preferences. Keep system/local fonts.

### 2. Replace navigation

- Rebuild `AppShell` using Sidebar header, content, menu, and footer composition.
- Preserve the five routes, active-page indication, household identity, About action, skip link, and local-only disclosure.
- Start desktop navigation expanded at the existing 248px width. Add an icon-rail collapse control and accessible tooltips for collapsed navigation items.
- Keep collapse state in React memory only; add no cookie or storage key.
- Preserve the 1024px desktop breakpoint. Below it, use a modal Sheet that closes after navigation, restores trigger focus, and closes when resizing to desktop.
- Replace the profile switcher with an avatar-bearing Select while retaining the visible “Demo perspective” label and conflict-disabled behavior.

### 3. Migrate shared controls across every screen

- Preserve the app-facing Button variants (`primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `danger`) through a thin adapter to shadcn styling. Use semantic links for navigation and buttons for actions.
- Replace `SelectField`’s native-event interface with typed options and `onValueChange(value)`. Options support labels, groups, disabled states, and optional avatar content. Update every caller explicitly.
- Preserve existing values and selection rules: 40 grouped avatar presets, active-member restrictions, historical archived selections, duplicate-payer disabling, and currency locking.
- Keep field labels, required indicators, help/error associations, and focus-to-first-invalid behavior working with custom select triggers.
- Replace shared dialog internals while retaining controlled open state, default/wide sizes, scrollable content, and feature-owned drafts.
- Use Alert Dialog for confirmations, initially focusing Cancel. Close only after successful actions; failed saves retain the dialog, error, and draft.
- Replace agreement menus with Dropdown Menu, including reliable menu-to-dialog focus handoff.
- Migrate setup choices, expense participant checkboxes, textareas, and single-selection toggle controls. Prevent deselecting the required current view/split choice.
- Preserve nested-overlay behavior: Escape closes the topmost overlay, dropdowns remain usable inside dialogs, and focus returns sensibly after deletion.

## Verification and review deliverable

- Update existing browser tests to operate custom selects through their triggers and options instead of native `selectOption` calls. Preserve existing behavioral assertions.
- Run unit/storage tests, the full browser suite, lint, typecheck, formatting checks, and the production static build.
- Verify navigation expansion/collapse, keyboard tooltips, mobile Sheet behavior, focus restoration, nested overlays, required fields, disabled options, and agreement menu actions.
- Recheck sample/empty setup, refresh persistence, failed-save retries, cross-tab conflicts, archived-member records, and expense split validation.
- Review screenshots at 375, 768, and 1280px, including long labels, 20 roommates, grouped avatar options, and the expense form.
- Deliver screenshots and a concise component replacement inventory for your next review. Record actual results and remaining limitations in `PLAN.md`; make a reviewable Git checkpoint without deploying.

## Boundaries and documentation

- Household actions, financial arithmetic, completion history, and persistence remain unchanged. No schema migration; retain `schemaVersion: 1` and `roomieos:v1`.
- Keep inline validation and storage feedback; do not introduce toast-only errors, dark mode, new product features, or network services.
- During implementation, narrowly amend the design guidance that currently specifies native selectors, documenting the approved shadcn controls and collapsible sidebar. Preserve unrelated requirements.
- This turn produces the plan only; implementation and repository documentation updates follow separately.

    # RoomieOS implementation plan
    
    **Last updated:** 24 November 2026
    
    **Status:** Milestone 5 implementation and verification complete. No deployment performed.
    
    **Current milestone:** Milestone 5 — integration complete.
    
    **Next milestone:** Milestone 6 — release verification and submission deliverables.
    
    **Delivery target:** Thursday, 26 November 2026; Friday, 27 November is the submission/fix buffer.
    
    ## 1. Purpose, authority and decisions
    
    Build a polished Next.js client-side prototype for ENTI 407. `docs/PRD.md` is authoritative for behavior; `docs/DESIGN.md` is authoritative for UI/UX. This document records approved architecture, sequencing and actual progress. It does not override those requirements.
    
    At plan approval, the repository contained documentation and a README, with no application scaffold. The foundation, household setup/persistence, chores, expenses, agreements and integrated dashboard are now implemented; see the progress record below for verification. Update this record after each working slice: check only completed work, record actual verification, and keep the current/next milestone accurate. Surface conflicts or new scope for user review rather than inventing requirements.
    
    ### Resolved requirements and defaults
    
    - **Approved Milestone 2 expansion:** The user raised the active-roommate limit from 5 to 20 and requested more avatar choices. The current limit is **2–20 active roommates**, with 40 named/grouped emoji presets plus initials. PRD and DESIGN version 1.1 now reflect this explicit user-approved change from the original 2–5 limit. Existing saved avatar values and `schemaVersion: 1` remain compatible.
    - **Backend conflict resolved:** The user selected the approved local-only scope. Use Next.js App Router without backend API routes, Server Actions, authentication or a database. Household operations run in the browser.
    - **History ordering:** Preserve completion events in append order; display newest first, as DESIGN specifies.
    - **Archived-member edge cases:** Historical records remain viewable and editable without losing member references. Before reopening an expense involving archived members, require their restoration. Before reopening a chore assigned to an archived member, require reassignment to an active member. Rotation can directly select the next active member.
    - **Design contrast:** Preserve the visual palette, but use sufficiently dark text variants where muted tokens fail contrast requirements.
    - **Priority:** All PRD must-haves remain MVP requirements. Defer photo uploads, drag-and-drop and decorative animation.
    
    ## 2. Architecture and state
    
    Use Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and `lucide-react`, with static deployment on Vercel.
    
    ### Application structure
    
    - **Routes (`src/app`):** `/` for Dashboard, plus `/welcome`, `/chores`, `/expenses`, `/agreements` and `/settings`. A client initialization gate shows loading until storage is read, then presents setup, recovery or the requested screen.
    - **Shared UI (`src/components`, `src/styles`):** App shell, page header, avatar/picker, fields, status pills, accessible dialogs, confirmations, notices and empty states. Desktop sidebar; mobile navigation drawer. Tables become cards on phones; Kanban scrolls within its own region.
    - **Feature modules (`src/features`):** Setup, household, chores, expenses, agreements and dashboard. Keep form drafts local to their feature.
    - **Domain utilities (`src/domain`):** Types, runtime validation, money parsing/allocation, balances, rotation, date helpers and sample generation. These functions must not depend on React or browser storage.
    - **State layer (`src/state`):** One client provider with typed domain actions and shared selectors. Route changes must preserve the provider. Keep browser storage access behind a small adapter.
    
    Follow the PRD's `AppState` model with `schemaVersion: 1`. Use stable IDs and member ordering; retain archived members. Persist facts, selected profile and settings. Calculate balances, transfer suggestions, overdue indicators and dashboard counts from those facts.
    "use client";
    
    import { useEffect, useId, useRef, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import { X } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./button";
    import { InlineNotice } from "./inline-notice";
    
    type DialogProps = {
      open: boolean;
      onClose: () => void;
      title: string;
      description?: string;
      children: ReactNode;
      variant?: "modal" | "drawer";
      id?: string;
      size?: "default" | "wide";
    };
    
    export function Dialog({
      open,
      onClose,
      title,
      description,
      children,
      variant = "modal",
      id,
      size = "default",
    }: DialogProps) {
      const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);
      const titleId = useId();
      const descriptionId = useId();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const dialog = dialogRef.current;
        if (!dialog || !open) return;
        const trigger =
          document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement
            ? document.activeElement
            : null;
        dialog.showModal();
        return () => {
          dialog.close();
          if (trigger?.isConnected) trigger.focus();
        };
      }, [open]);
    
      return (
        <dialog
          ref={dialogRef}
          id={id}
          aria-labelledby={titleId}
          aria-describedby={description ? descriptionId : undefined}
          onCancel={(event) => {
            event.preventDefault();
            onClose();
          }}
          className={`fixed flex-col overflow-hidden border border-line bg-page p-0 text-ink shadow-xl ${variant === "drawer" ? "inset-y-0 left-0 m-0 h-dvh max-h-dvh w-80 max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] rounded-r-xl" : `inset-0 m-auto max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] rounded-xl ${size === "wide" ? "max-w-2xl" : "max-w-lg"}`}`}
        >
          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-between gap-4 border-b border-line px-5 py-3">
            <h2 id={titleId} className="min-w-0 break-words text-lg font-semibold">
              {title}
            </h2>
            <Button
              variant="ghost"
              onClick={onClose}
              aria-label={`Close ${title}`}
              title="Close"
              size="icon"
            >
              <X aria-hidden="true" className="size-5" />
            </Button>
          </div>
          <div className="overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-5">
            {description && (
              <p id={descriptionId} className="mb-5 break-words text-sm text-muted">
                {description}
              </p>
            )}
            {children}
          </div>
        </dialog>
      );
    }
    
    export function ConfirmDialog({
      open,
      onClose,
      onConfirm,
      title,
      description,
      confirmLabel,
      destructive = false,
      error,
    }: Omit<DialogProps, "children" | "variant" | "id"> & {
      onConfirm: () => void;
      confirmLabel: string;
      destructive?: boolean;
      error?: string;
    }) {
      return (
        <Dialog
          open={open}
          onClose={onClose}
          title={title}
          description={description}
        >
          {error && (
            <div className="mb-4">
              <InlineNotice tone="error">{error}</InlineNotice>
            </div>
          )}
          <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-end gap-3">
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button
              variant={destructive ? "danger" : "primary"}
              onClick={onConfirm}
            >
              {confirmLabel}
            </Button>
          </div>
        </Dialog>
      );
    }

    ---
    title: Server and Client Components
    description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.
    related:
      title: Next Steps
      description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.
      links:
        - app/api-reference/directives/use-client
        - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary
    ---
    
    By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.
    
    This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.
    
    > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).
    
    ## When to use Server and Client Components?
    
    The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.
    
    Use **Client Components** when you need:
    
    - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.
    - [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.
    - Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `navigator.geolocation`, etc.
    - [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).
    
    Use **Server Components** when you need:
    
    - Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.
    - Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.
    - Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.
    - Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.
    
    For example, the `<Page>` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `<LikeButton>` which handles client-side interactivity.

    }) {
      const { id } = await params
      const post = await getPost(id)
    
      return (
        <div>
          <main>
            <h1>{post.title}</h1>
            {/* ... */}
            <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />

        "use client";
        import { isValidElement, type ReactNode } from "react";
        import { Label } from "./primitives/label";
        import { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectValue, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectGroup, SelectLabel } from "./primitives/select";
        export type SelectOption = {value:string;label:ReactNode;disabled?:boolean;group?:string};
        type OptionInput = SelectOption | false | null | undefined | OptionInput[];
        export function selectOptions(...inputs:OptionInput[]):SelectOption[] { return inputs.flatMap(input => Array.isArray(input) ? selectOptions(...input) : input ? [input] : []); }
        function text(node:ReactNode):string { if (typeof node === "string" || typeof node === "number") return String(node); if(Array.isArray(node))return node.map(text).join(""); if(isValidElement<{children?:ReactNode}>(node))return text(node.props.children); return ""; }
        export function SelectField({id,label,help,error,options,value,onValueChange,disabled,required,name,className,"aria-label":ariaLabel}: {id:string;label:string;help?:string;error?:string;options:SelectOption[];value:string;onValueChange:(value:string)=>void;disabled?:boolean;required?:boolean;name?:string;className?:string;"aria-label"?:string}) {
         const groups=Array.from(new Set(options.map(o=>o.group)));
         return <div className="min-w-0 space-y-2"><Label htmlFor={id} className="block text-sm font-medium">{label}</Label>
         <Select value={value} onValueChange={v=>{if(v!==null)onValueChange(v);}} disabled={disabled} required={required} name={name} items={options.map(o=>({value:o.value,label:text(o.label)}))}>
         <SelectTrigger id={id} aria-label={ariaLabel} aria-invalid={Boolean(error)} aria-describedby={[help&&`${id}-help`,error&&`${id}-error`].filter(Boolean).join(" ")||undefined} className={`w-full min-w-0 ${className??""}`}><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
         <SelectContent align="start" alignItemWithTrigger={false} className="max-h-72 max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]">
         {groups.map((group,i)=><SelectGroup key={group??i}>{group&&<SelectLabel>{group}</SelectLabel>}{options.filter(o=>o.group===group).map(o=><SelectItem key={o.value} value={o.value} disabled={o.disabled} data-value={o.value}>{o.label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectGroup>)}
         </SelectContent></Select>
         {help&&<p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted">{help}</p>}{error&&<p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-danger">{error}</p>}</div>;

        import * as D from "./primitives/dialog";

        import * as S from "./primitives/sheet";
        type DialogProps={open:boolean;onClose:()=>void;title:string;description?:string;children:ReactNode;variant?:"modal"|"drawer";id?:string;size?:"default"|"wide"};
        export function Dialog({open,onClose,title,description,children,variant="modal",id,size="default"}:DialogProps){
         const trigger=useRef<HTMLElement|null>(null);
         const capture=()=>{trigger.current=document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement?document.activeElement:null;return true;};
         const restore=()=>{if(trigger.current?.isConnected){trigger.current.focus();return false;}return true;};
         if(variant==="drawer")return <S.Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={v=>{if(!v)onClose();}}><S.SheetContent id={id} side="left" className="w-80 max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] overflow-y-auto" initialFocus={capture} finalFocus={restore}><S.SheetHeader><S.SheetTitle>{title}</S.SheetTitle>{description&&<S.SheetDescription>{description}</S.SheetDescription>}</S.SheetHeader><div className="p-5">{children}</div></S.SheetContent></S.Sheet>;
         return <D.Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={v=>{if(!v)onClose();}}><D.DialogContent id={id} showCloseButton={false} initialFocus={capture} finalFocus={restore} className={`flex max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] flex-col gap-0 overflow-hidden p-0 ${size==="wide"?"sm:max-w-2xl":"sm:max-w-lg"}`}>
         <D.DialogHeader className="shrink-0 flex-row items-center justify-between border-b border-line px-5 py-3"><D.DialogTitle className="min-w-0 break-words text-lg font-semibold">{title}</D.DialogTitle><Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label={`Close ${title}`} onClick={onClose}><X aria-hidden="true" className="size-5"/></Button></D.DialogHeader>
         <div className="overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-5">{description&&<D.DialogDescription className="mb-5">{description}</D.DialogDescription>}{children}</div>
         </D.DialogContent></D.Dialog>;
        }
        export function ConfirmDialog({open,onClose,onConfirm,title,description,confirmLabel,destructive=false,error}:Omit<DialogProps,"children"|"variant"|"id">&{onConfirm:()=>void;confirmLabel:string;destructive?:boolean;error?:string}){
         const cancel=useRef<HTMLButtonElement|null>(null);const trigger=useRef<HTMLElement|null>(null);
         return <A.AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={v=>{if(!v)onClose();}}><A.AlertDialogContent initialFocus={()=>{trigger.current=document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement?document.activeElement:null;return cancel.current;}} finalFocus={()=>{if(trigger.current?.isConnected){trigger.current.focus();return false;}return true;}} className="max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] overflow-y-auto data-[size=default]:max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] data-[size=default]:sm:max-w-lg p-5">
         <A.AlertDialogHeader className="place-items-start text-left"><A.AlertDialogTitle>{title}</A.AlertDialogTitle><A.AlertDialogDescription>{description}</A.AlertDialogDescription></A.AlertDialogHeader>{error&&<InlineNotice tone="error">{error}</InlineNotice>}
         <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-end gap-3"><Button ref={cancel} variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button><Button variant={destructive?"danger":"primary"} onClick={onConfirm}>{confirmLabel}</Button></div></A.AlertDialogContent></A.AlertDialog>;
        }

    function Sidebar({
      side = "left",
      variant = "sidebar",
      collapsible = "offcanvas",
      className,
      children,
      dir,
      ...props
    }: React.ComponentProps<"div"> & {
      side?: "left" | "right"
      variant?: "sidebar" | "floating" | "inset"
      collapsible?: "offcanvas" | "icon" | "none"
    }) {
      const { isMobile, state, openMobile, setOpenMobile } = useSidebar()
    
      if (collapsible === "none") {
        return (
          <div
            data-slot="sidebar"
            className={cn(
              "flex h-full w-(--sidebar-width) flex-col bg-sidebar text-sidebar-foreground",
              className
            )}
            {...props}
          >
            {children}
          </div>
        )
      }
    
      if (isMobile) {
        return (
          <Sheet open={openMobile} onOpenChange={setOpenMobile} {...props}>
            <SheetContent
              dir={dir}
              data-sidebar="sidebar"
              data-slot="sidebar"
              data-mobile="true"
              className="w-(--sidebar-width) bg-sidebar p-0 text-sidebar-foreground [&>button]:hidden"
              style={
                {

            </SheetContent>
          </Sheet>
        )

      }

          {...props}

            {children}

        import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
        export async function selectControl(locator:Locator, option:string|{label:string}) {
         await locator.click();
         const options=locator.page().getByRole("option");
         if(typeof option === "string") await options.filter({visible:true}).locator(`and-nothing`).count().catch(()=>{});
         const item=typeof option === "string" ? locator.page().locator('[role="option"]').filter({visible:true}).filter({has:undefined}) : options.getByText(option.label,{exact:true});
         if(typeof option === "string") await locator.page().locator(`[role="option"][data-value=${JSON.stringify(option)}]`).click(); else await item.click();
        }
        export async function expectControlValue(locator:Locator,value:string|RegExp) {
         if(await locator.evaluate(el=>el.tagName==="BUTTON")) await expect(locator).toHaveAttribute("data-value",value); else await expect(locator).toHaveValue(value);
        }
        export function getDialog(scope:Page|Locator,options?:{name?:string|RegExp;exact?:boolean}) {return scope.getByRole("dialog",options).or(scope.getByRole("alertdialog",options));}
        export async function selectItems(locator:Locator) {await locator.click();return locator.page().getByRole("option");}

    test("about dialog traps keyboard focus, closes with Escape and restores focus", async ({
      page,
    }) => {
      await page.goto("/");
      await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
      await page
        .getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true })
        .filter({ visible: true })
        .click();
      const dialog = getDialog(page, {
        name: "About RoomieOS",
        exact: true,
      });
      const close = dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Close About RoomieOS" });
      await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
      await expect(close).toBeFocused();
      await page.keyboard.press("Tab");
      // Native dialogs may focus the document between cycles, but never an outside control.
      expect(
        await page.evaluate(
          () =>
            document.activeElement === document.body ||
            Boolean(document.activeElement?.closest("dialog[open]")),
        ),
      ).toBe(true);
      await page.keyboard.press("Shift+Tab");
      await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
      await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();
      const expectedFocus =
        page.viewportSize()!.width >= 1024
          ? page
              .getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true })
              .filter({ visible: true })
          : page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      await expect(expectedFocus).toBeFocused();
    });

    import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
    export async function selectControl(
      locator: Locator,
      option: string | { label: string },
    ) {
      await locator.click();
      const options = locator.page().getByRole("option");
      const item = options.getByText(
        typeof option === "string" ? option : option.label,
        { exact: true },
      );
      if (typeof option === "string")
        await locator
          .page()
          .locator(`[role="option"][data-value=${JSON.stringify(option)}]`)
          .filter({ visible: true })
          .click();
      else await item.click();
    }
    export async function expectControlValue(
      locator: Locator,
      value: string | RegExp,
    ) {
      if (await locator.evaluate((el) => el.tagName === "BUTTON"))
        await expect(locator).toHaveAttribute("data-value", value);
      else await expect(locator).toHaveValue(value);
    }
    export function getDialog(
      scope: Page | Locator,
      options?: { name?: string | RegExp; exact?: boolean },
    ) {
      return scope
        .getByRole("dialog", options)
        .or(scope.getByRole("alertdialog", options));
    }
    export async function selectItems(locator: Locator) {
      await locator.click();
      return locator.page().getByRole("option");
    }

    import { isValidElement, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import { Label } from "./primitives/label";
    import {
      Select,
      SelectTrigger,
      SelectValue,
      SelectContent,
      SelectItem,
      SelectGroup,
      SelectLabel,
    } from "./primitives/select";
    export type SelectOption = {
      value: string;
      label: ReactNode;
      disabled?: boolean;
      group?: string;
    };
    type OptionInput = SelectOption | false | null | undefined | OptionInput[];
    export function selectOptions(...inputs: OptionInput[]): SelectOption[] {
      return inputs.flatMap((input) =>
        Array.isArray(input) ? selectOptions(...input) : input ? [input] : [],
      );
    }
    function text(node: ReactNode): string {
      if (typeof node === "string" || typeof node === "number") return String(node);
      if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.map(text).join("");
      if (isValidElement<{ children?: ReactNode }>(node))
        return text(node.props.children);
      return "";
    }

        test("navigation adapts, collapsed labels have tooltips, and perspective selection works by keyboard", async ({page},testInfo)=>{
         await page.addInitScript(state=>localStorage.setItem("roomieos:v1",JSON.stringify(state)),createSampleHousehold(new Date()));
         await page.goto("/");
         const original=await page.evaluate(()=>localStorage.getItem("roomieos:v1"));
         if(page.viewportSize()!.width>=1024){
          await page.getByRole("button",{name:"Collapse sidebar"}).click();
          await expect(page.locator('[data-slot="sidebar"][data-state="collapsed"]')).toBeVisible();
          await page.getByRole("link",{name:"Chores",exact:true}).hover();
          await expect(page.getByRole("tooltip",{name:"Chores",exact:true})).toBeVisible();
          await page.screenshot({path:testInfo.outputPath("sidebar-collapsed.png"),fullPage:true});
          expect(await page.evaluate(()=>localStorage.getItem("roomieos:v1"))).toBe(original);
          expect(await page.context().cookies()).toEqual([]);
          await page.getByRole("button",{name:"Expand sidebar"}).click();
         }else{
          await page.getByRole("button",{name:"Open navigation"}).click();
          await expect(page.getByRole("dialog",{name:"Navigation",exact:true})).toBeVisible();
          await page.screenshot({path:testInfo.outputPath("navigation-sheet.png"),fullPage:true});
          await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
          await expect(page.getByRole("button",{name:"Open navigation"})).toBeFocused();
         }
         const perspective=page.getByRole("combobox",{name:"Switch demo perspective"});
         await perspective.focus();await page.keyboard.press("ArrowDown");
         await expect(page.getByRole("listbox")).toBeVisible();
         await page.keyboard.press("End");await page.keyboard.press("Enter");
         await expect(perspective).toHaveAttribute("data-value","sam");
         await expect(perspective).toBeFocused();
         await page.screenshot({path:testInfo.outputPath("dashboard-refreshed.png"),fullPage:true});
         await page.reload();await expect(perspective).toHaveAttribute("data-value","sam");
         if(page.viewportSize()!.width>=1024) await expect(page.getByRole("button",{name:"Collapse sidebar"})).toBeVisible();
         expect(await page.evaluate(()=>document.documentElement.scrollWidth>innerWidth)).toBe(false);
        });
